newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Islamist party change name.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Islamist party change name.

text.p: One of Algeria's two legal Islamist parties, Nahda Islamic Movement, announced on Saturday it was changing its name in line with a new law banning political parties based on Islam.
Party leader Abdallah Djaballah said in a statement the party was renamed Nahda Movement by the group's top policy-making body, the National Shoura Majlis, during a two-day meeting in Algiers.
"The Majlis, which has undertaken its full responsibilities to pursue the path of political and peaceful change...announces the party was renamed Nahda Movement," he said.
Algeria's government-appointed Transitional National Council, a quasi-parliament, approved a party law on February 18 banning political parties from having a political paltform based on religion.

The bill was seen as a tool handed to President Liamine Zeroual to carry out his attempt to realign the political field after the annulment of a general election in 1992 when radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) was poised to win.
Zeroual on Friday set June 5 as a date for the first parliamentary elections since 1992.
Djaballah's statement said the Majlis also asked the party's leadership to come up with a plan on how to meet the law's requirements.
The law gives Nahda and the second legal Islamist party, Hamas, two months to change their manifestos to be in line with the legislation. Political sources expect Hamas to follow suit.
Algeria plunged into violence when the 1992 polls were scrapped and FIS banned. About 60,000 people have died since then in the strife pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces.
